outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) The agent’s EPUB3 link text in the output slightly truncates the on-page label (missing the trailing “!”). This is minor and doesn’t affect the availability determination. 

Critical issues: (1) Release Date and Last Update are core required deliverables, with a strict constraint to use the Gutenberg page’s own “Release Date” and “Last Update” labels and to preserve displayed dates exactly. The DOM evidence provided for the agent’s session shows no “Release Date” field and no “Last Update” field visible anywhere, yet the agent outputs specific dates (“Release Date: Jun 1, 1998” and “Last Update: Sep 1, 2026”). With no DOM support and no stated access blocker, these values are ungrounded/fabricated relative to the recorded evidence, and they directly violate the task’s key constraint. 

What was done correctly: The agent did access the correct eBook 1342 page. Author (“Austen, Jane, 1775-1817”) and Language (“English”) are supported by the metadata table in DOM state 1. Format availability for EPUB3 and Download HTML (zip) is supported (both labels appear as links in DOM state 1). The agent also correctly notes that the specific label “Plain Text (accessible)” is not shown in the provided DOM (only “Plain Text” is shown). 

Overall outcome: Because two of the four required metadata fields (Release Date and Last Update) are presented as specific values without evidentiary basis in the DOM snapshots—and these are explicitly hard constraints—the agent did not successfully complete the task as requested, even though it correctly handled author/language and the three format checks.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to open Project Gutenberg eBook #1342 (Pride and Prejudice) and accurately record four on-page metadata fields (Author, Release Date, Last Update, Language) plus whether three specific format labels (EPUB3, Plain Text (accessible), Download HTML (zip)) are available—without downloading anything and preserving the page’s labels/dates exactly. A reasonable user would not be flexible about incorrect or fabricated Release Date/Last Update values, since those are explicitly required to come from the Gutenberg page labels, not general knowledge.
